findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10 schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed keys, evaluating to constant string `"[object Object]"` instead of a dynamic catchall; intended permissive schema for credential-sync mode is not achieved and only `access_token` is validated. Should use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())`.

googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:96 saves the full `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`) to the credential `key` column instead of `key.data`, corrupting stored Google credentials so subsequent token refreshes/usage fail.

zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:90 passes `credentialId` to `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` as the `userId` parameter instead of `credential.userId` like every other call site, causing the credential sync endpoint to receive the wrong identifier and fail to map to the user.

.env.example comment states the AES256 key "must be 32 bytes" but recommends `openssl rand -base64 24`, which yields 24 random bytes (32 base64 chars); this will fail at runtime if `symmetricDecrypt` expects a 32-byte key. Should use `openssl rand -base64 32` or `openssl rand 32`.

salesforce CalendarService.ts:80 uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` which is fragile; HTTP/2 responses often have empty `statusText` and status text varies by server. Should use `response.ok` or `response.status === 200`.

salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-99 executes a token-refresh network call unconditionally inside the `conn` Promise on every service instantiation instead of only when the access token has expired, adding latency, an extra OAuth call per operation, and risking rate limits.
app-credential.ts:18-39 has no HTTP method check; this state-changing endpoint accepts GET/DELETE/PUT/etc. and should be restricted to POST.
app-credential.ts:21-25 compares webhook secret with `!==`, which is timing-unsafe; should use a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to avoid leaking the secret via timing.

app-credential.ts:29,72-74 does not wrap `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` in try/catch; malformed bodies or decryption failures produce unhandled 500s instead of controlled 400s.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7-13 fetch to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no `response.ok` check, no Content-Type header, and no error handling; a non-OK or non-conforming response is returned as if valid and may be misinterpreted by callers' error handlers.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7-13 request to the external credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no authentication header or signature; any party able to reach the endpoint can impersonate users. Should send a signed payload or bearer token.

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 defaults missing `refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"`; this sentinel can mask real missing-token errors and, if persisted, will be used as a real refresh token on the next refresh attempt, causing opaque failures.

office365calendar CalendarService.ts and zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts have dead code after `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure; previous graceful handling paths (e.g., O365's `console.error` logging) are removed and now surface as thrown errors.

constants.ts:102-103 types `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `string | undefined` instead of boolean; consumers treating it as a strict boolean (e.g., boolean prop or zod schema) will break. Should cast with `!!` or `Boolean(...)`.
No unit/integration tests added for the new `app-credential` webhook, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, or `refreshOAuthTokens` despite handling credential creation, decryption, and external HTTP calls.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10 schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed keys, evaluating to constant string `"[object Object]"` instead of a dynamic catchall; intended permissive schema for credential-sync mode is not achieved and only `access_token` is validated. Should use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the Zod schema is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(), })`. The computed property keys are evaluated immediately and become a single constant string key (e.g., "[object Object]"/"ZodString"), not a dynamic “any key”/catchall. That means `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will generally fail for normal OAuth token responses (which won’t contain that literal key), breaking the intended permissive validation in credential-sync mode. Using `.passthrough()`/`.catchall(...)` (or a `z.record`) is the correct approach for arbitrary keys.

Should use `openssl rand -base64 32` or `openssl rand 32`.

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example` the new comments for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` explicitly say the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256", but the suggested generation command is `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes (then base64-encodes them to a 32-character string). That is a concrete inconsistency in the diff and can lead operators to generate a key that is not 32 bytes as stated, potentially breaking encryption/decryption depending on how `symmetricDecrypt` interprets the key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts:18-39 has no HTTP method check; this state-changing endpoint accepts GET/DELETE/PUT/etc. and should be restricted to POST.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` API route, the `handler` performs state-changing operations (decrypts credentials, then `prisma.credential.update`/`create`) without checking `req.method`. Next.js API routes accept all HTTP methods unless explicitly gated, so GET/PUT/DELETE/etc. will reach this logic. While non-POST requests may fail later at `zod.parse(req.body)` (likely throwing and returning 500), the lack of an explicit method restriction is a real, verifiable defect for a webhook endpoint intended to be POST-only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts:21-25 compares webhook secret with `!==`, which is timing-unsafe; should use a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to avoid leaking the secret via timing.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authentication check directly compares the provided header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`. For string secrets, normal equality checks are not constant-time and can theoretically leak information via timing differences. This is a verifiable security issue in the diff; a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on Buffers of equal length) would avoid that class of side-channel.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7-13 fetch to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no `response.ok` check, no Content-Type header, and no error handling; a non-OK or non-conforming response is returned as if valid and may be misinterpreted by callers' error handlers.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately `return response;` without checking `response.ok`, without parsing/validating the body, and without any try/catch. This means non-2xx responses (or error pages / unexpected payloads) are returned to callers as if they were usable results, which can be misinterpreted downstream. The comment about missing `Content-Type` is less definitive because `URLSearchParams` often causes fetch implementations to set an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content-type automatically, but the lack of status/shape validation and error handling is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7-13 request to the external credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no authentication header or signature; any party able to reach the endpoint can impersonate users. Should send a signed payload or bearer token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code POSTs to the external sync endpoint with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and does not include any authentication material (no shared secret header, signature, bearer token, etc.). This means the receiving endpoint has no built-in way (from this client) to verify the request originated from Cal.com, so if that endpoint is reachable by others and relies on these fields to act on behalf of a user, it is susceptible to impersonation/abuse. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change Office365CalendarService’s behavior: it replaces a `safeParse` + conditional `console.error` path with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which explicitly `throw`s if parsing fails. However, the proposed finding is not verifiably correct as stated: (1) there is no “dead code after `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws” in `office365calendar`—the prior `if (!tokenResponse.success) { console.error(...) }` block was removed, so there’s no unreachable/dead code left behind; and (2) `zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts` is not shown/modified in this diff—`office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` is changed and it does not call `parseRefreshTokenResponse` at all. Thus the claim does not match the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: constants.ts:102-103 types `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `string | undefined` instead of boolean; consumers treating it as a strict boolean (e.g., boolean prop or zod schema) will break. Should cast with `!!` or `Boolean(...)`.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `constants.ts:102-103` and claims `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is typed as `string | undefined`, but `constants.ts` is not included/changed anywhere in the provided diff, and the diff does not show how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined or typed. The diff only shows new/updated consumers importing and using it in boolean contexts, which is not sufficient to verify a type mismatch. Therefore the issue is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit/integration tests added for the new `app-credential` webhook, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, or `refreshOAuthTokens` despite handling credential creation, decryption, and external HTTP calls.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new API/webhook logic and helper utilities, but it does not include any test files/changes. While that absence is observable in this patch, “no tests were added” is a process/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete bug, security flaw, or correctness defect introduced by the code itself, and the diff provides no requirement that tests must be added alongside such changes.
